q: 1. The state of pure shear stress is produced by
options: tension in one direction and equal compression in perpendicular direction
equal tensions in two directions at right angles
equal compression in two directions at right angles
explain: Pure shear at 45° is equivalent to equal tension and compression at right angles on the original planes; hence tension in one direction with equal compression perpendicular to it produces a state of pure shear.

q: 2. The direction of normal stress is
explain: By definition, normal stress acts perpendicular (normal) to the surface of the cross-section or failure plane.

q: 3. The percentage elongation of a material from a direct tensile test indicates
explain: High percentage elongation is a primary indicator that a material is ductile and can undergo significant plastic deformation.

q: 4. Along the neutral axis of a simply supported beam
explain: By definition, the neutral axis is the layer in a beam where bending-induced longitudinal strain is zero — fibres there neither stretch nor compress.

q: 5. What is tenancy?
explain: Tenacity (often misspelled as tenancy) refers to the ultimate tensile strength of a material.

q: 6. Due to torsion moment beam get
explain: While bending moments cause curvature (bending), torsional moments specifically cause the cross-sections to rotate or twist relative to each other.

q: 7. Stress concentration near the void is ................ as compared to solid portion.
explain: Voids or discontinuities disrupt the flow of stress lines, causing them to 'bunch up' and increase the local stress intensity.

q: 8. For no torsion, the plane of bending should
options: be parallel to one of the principal axes
pass through shear center of section
pass through neutral axis of the section
pass through cg of the section
explain: To avoid inducing torsion in an unsymmetrical section, the plane of the transverse load (bending) must pass through the shear center of the section.

q: 9. An element is subjected to two equal and like stress σ, on two mutually perpendicular planes. The shape of the Mohr's circle will be
explain: When both principal stresses are equal (σ1=σ2=σ), the Mohr's circle degenerates to a single point on the normal-stress axis, since there is no shear stress on any plane.

q: 10. In rectangular columns (cross-section b × h), the core is a
options: rectangle of lengths b/2 and h/2
rhombus of diagonals b/3 and h/3
explain: For a rectangular column b×h, the core (middle-third rule region) is a rhombus with diagonals equal to b/3 and h/3.

q: 11. When a rectangular beam is loaded transversely, the maximum compressive force develops on
explain: For a simply supported beam under transverse load, sagging occurs, which puts the top fibers in compression and the bottom fibers in tension.

q: 12. The ratio of maximum and average shear stresses on a circular section is
explain: For a circular section, the ratio of maximum to average shear stress is 4/3, a standard result from integrating the parabolic-type shear distribution over a circle.

q: 13. The residual stress in a member is
options: the stress due to the loading on the member
the average of initial and final stresses
instantaneous stress due to sudden loading
explain: Residual stress is the internal stress remaining in a member after all external loads have been removed, arising from non-uniform plastic deformation — best described as a 'deformation stress'.

q: 14. The modulus of elasticity for mild steel is approximately equal to
explain: The Young's modulus (modulus of elasticity) of mild steel is approximately 200-210 kN/mm² (GPa), a standard material property value.

q: 15. When a bar is cooled to −5°C, it will develop
explain: As with heating, if the bar is free (unrestrained) while being cooled, it can contract freely and no internal stress is induced.

q: 16. A bar of copper and steel form a composite system, which is heated to a temperature of 40. The stress induced in the copper bar will be
explain: Since copper has a higher coefficient of thermal expansion than steel, in a bonded composite bar heated together, copper is restrained from expanding as much as it wants by the steel, inducing compressive stress in the copper.

q: 17. The ratio of bulk modulus to Young's modulus for a Poisson's ratio of 0.25 will be
explain: Using K/E = 1/[3(1−2μ)], substituting μ=0.25 gives K/E = 1/[3(0.5)] = 2/3.

q: 18. The line showing the variations of stress function at a given point due to a unit load moving on a span is known as
explain: This is the formal definition of an influence line. It tracks how a single 'unit' load affects one specific point as that load changes position.

q: 19. The neutral axis of any section is
options: the axis passing through middle point of the height
the line of intersection of neutral plane with cross-section
the axis about which the moment of inertia is minimum
explain: The neutral axis is defined as the line of intersection between the neutral plane (zero-strain plane) of the beam and its cross-section.

q: 20. Maximum principal stress theory for the failure of a material at elastic point is known as
explain: The maximum principal stress theory of failure is also known as Rankine's theory.

q: 21. The Poisson's ratio is the ratio of
options: Yong's modulus elasticity to modulus of rigidity
explain: Poisson's ratio is, by definition, the ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal (axial) strain under uniaxial loading.

q: 22. The strain energy stored in a body, when suddenly loaded, is ............. the strain energy stored when same load is applied gradually.
explain: A suddenly applied load causes twice the stress/deformation of a gradual load, and since strain energy ∝ (deformation)², the stored energy becomes four times as much.

q: 23. To avoid any possibility of tension occurring in masonry structures, the resultant of various forces at any level must through
options: middle third of the width or depth of the section
explain: The 'middle third rule' requires the resultant force to pass within the middle third of the section width/depth to prevent tensile stress in masonry (which cannot resist tension).

q: 24. Every material obeys the Hooke's law within its
explain: Hooke's law (stress directly proportional to strain) strictly holds only up to the limit of proportionality on the stress-strain curve.

q: 25. In a bar of large length when held vertically and subjected to a load at its lower end, its own-weight, produces additional stress. The maximum stress will be
options: at every point of the bar
explain: The internal axial force (and hence stress) accumulates from the free lower end upward due to self-weight, so the maximum total stress (applied load + accumulated self-weight) occurs at the top, built-in cross-section.

q: 26. The shear flow in a section can be defined as
options: total shear stress at a point
explain: Shear flow ($q$) is the shear force per unit length along a cross-section ($q = 	au \cdot t$).

q: 27. When a thin cylindrical shell is subjected to internal fluid pressure, which of the following stress is developed in its wall ?
explain: Internal pressure in cylinders creates both hoop (circumferential) and longitudinal stresses.

q: 28. The neutral axis of the cross-section of a beam is that axis at which the bending stress is
explain: By definition, the neutral axis is the axis in the cross-section where bending stress (and strain) is zero.

q: 29. A beam of uniform strength may be obtained by
options: keeping the width uniform and varying the depth
keeping the depth uniform and varying the width
varying the width and depth both
explain: A beam of uniform strength can be achieved by varying depth alone, width alone, or both together, as long as the section modulus varies appropriately with the moment — hence any of these approaches works.

q: 30. The stress at which the extension of the material takes place more quickly as compared to the increase in load, is called
explain: This describes the yield point, where strain increases disproportionately compared to the increase in load/stress.

q: 31. The compression test is carried on ............. materials.
explain: Compression tests are the standard test method for brittle materials (like cast iron, concrete), which are weak in tension but strong in compression.

q: 32. If a material has identical properties in all directions, it is said to be
explain: Isotropic means having identical mechanical properties in every direction at a point, as opposed to homogeneous (uniform properties throughout the material, but possibly directionally dependent).

q: 33. How does the Young's Modulus vary with increase in temperature?
explain: Young's modulus of most metals decreases as temperature increases, due to increased atomic vibration weakening interatomic bonding stiffness.

q: 34. A plane section before twisting will remain plane after twisting if the cross-section is
explain: Only circular (and hollow circular) shafts maintain plane cross-sections after twisting because of their rotational symmetry; non-circular sections warp under torsion.

q: 35. The ratio of the length and diameter of a simply supported uniform circular beam which experiences maximum bending stress equal to tensile stress due to same load at its mid span is
explain: Equating the bending stress formula (from flexure) to the direct tensile stress formula (from axial elongation test) for the same circular bar and load leads to a length-to-diameter ratio of 1/2.

q: 36. In a shaft, the shear stress is not directly proportional to
explain: From τ = Gθr/L, shear stress is proportional to radius, angle of twist, and modulus of rigidity, but is inversely (not directly) proportional to the length of the shaft.

q: 37. Compression members always tend to buckle in the direction of the
options: perpendicular to the axis of load
explain: A compression member buckles about the axis corresponding to its least radius of gyration (weakest bending stiffness direction), since that requires the smallest load to induce instability.

q: 38. The direct stress induced in a long column is ............. as compared to bending stress.
explain: For long, slender columns where buckling (bending) effects dominate, the direct (axial) stress component is comparatively negligible relative to the bending stress induced by buckling.

q: 39. A column that fails due to direct stress, is called
explain: A column that fails primarily by crushing (direct compressive stress reaching material strength, without significant buckling) is classified as a short column.
